To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

equity carve-outs, on average, are associated with positive share price reactions, that the positive share price reactions are related to the announcement that a subsidiary will become a separate publicly-traded company, that the share price reactions are not related to the announcement of the offering itself, that the positive reactions are not related, on average, to the amount of equity sold, to the size of the subsidiary, to the amount raised by the offering, or to the parent firm’s financial leverage, and that the positive

equity carve-outs have positive average abnormal gains associated therewith, and that the average abnormal gain associated with an announcement of an equity carve-out is significantly larger than the average abnormal loss associated with an announcement that a parent is making a seasoned equity offering.
equity carve-outs are associated with significant positive average abnormal returns and that this result is robust to a variety of tests.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: why is the average abnormal gain of equity carve-out announcements different from the average abnormal loss associated with seasoned equity offerings?
the effects of corporate restructuring on the value of equity of parent firms.
the effects of equity carve-outs on parent firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
equity carve-outs are not the same as parent equity offerings.

equity carve-outs are a form of corporate restructuring, and that the average abnormal gain associated with equity carve-out announcements is consistent with the hypothesis that the gains represent the value of the restructuring.
equity carve-outs and public offerings of parent firms’ common stock are not the same thing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
equity carve-outs are a corporate restructuring strategy which, in general, is associated with a significant positive share price reaction.
equity carve-outs are a corporate restructuring technique which is not used for its own sake.
equity carve-outs are a form of corporate restructuring that is associated with a positive share price reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
equity carve-outs are an important form of corporate restructuring.
equity carve-outs are a form of corporate restructuring that is distinct from the parent firm issuing equity.
equity carve-outs and public offerings of parent stock are not equivalent.
